messages.author: 98a4bbcd9a331950
messages.subject: Types of sums of Squares...
parts:
Hi Ian,

Deducer is a great GUI, and I love the new ggplot2 GUI! Superb work.

I hate to bring up such a controversial old chestnut, but would it be
possible to include Type I sums of squares as an option in Deducer's
modelling facilities? And, if not already available in Deducer, the
ability to set a particular type as a default option for all relevant
analyses?

There is a sizeable community of statisticians who strongly prefer the
logic of the Type I sum of squares - I would like to present Deducer
as a useful R GUI to others within my organisation, but the lack of
Type I SS goes against the accepted philosophy here.

I can appreciate the conservative nature of the Type II SS in the
context of ANOVA (I.e., analysis of designed experiments with
categorical predictors only) but in, say a multivariate regression,
Type II does not seem like the best choice at all...

Cheers,

Alec Zwart

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Types of sums of Squares...
parts:
I don't like type I ssq at all, but you should be able to use them if
you wish. I will implement this next time I alter the modeling dialogs
(which may be some time from now). As a general design principle I'd
like to stay away from preferences that change the default types of
analysis because then users can perform the same actions and get
different results.

ian
